title: The node drain that never finishes
scenario: "The AKS upgrade has been stuck for an hour on 'draining node'. The cluster autoscaler cannot remove the extra node either. Nothing is broken — but nothing moves." — Platform on-call
mission: Find why voluntary disruptions are blocked and fix the chart so every component has a PodDisruptionBudget that protects availability without blocking drains — in every environment.
objectives: Compute ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS from a PDB and the real replica count
Make chart behaviour depend on per-environment values
Validate a chart offline with helm lint and helm template

prerequisites.notes: Works with the platform stopped: only helm and git are needed.

steps.title: Render dev
steps.detail: Render the chart exactly as Argo CD would for dev and find every PodDisruptionBudget and HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
steps.command: helm template customer-portal gitops/charts/customer-portal -f gitops/envs/dev/platform.values.yaml -f gitops/envs/dev/values.yaml

steps.title: Do the arithmetic
steps.detail: For each PDB: minimum replicas in this environment minus minAvailable = allowed disruptions. What happens at 0?

steps.title: Design the fix
steps.detail: Both api and web need a budget; each budget must select only its own pods; the budgets must sit behind a values switch named pdb.enabled (default true).

steps.title: Validate offline
steps.detail: Lint and render dev and prod, then render with --set pdb.enabled=false.

steps.title: Commit on a branch
steps.detail: Commit the chart change; open a PR so CI runs helm lint too.

criteria.text: helm lint passes for dev and prod
Exactly one PodDisruptionBudget selects only the API pods (dev and prod)
Exactly one PodDisruptionBudget selects only the web pods (dev and prod)
Every budget allows at least 1 voluntary disruption at each environment's minimum replicas

expectedResult: Node drains and autoscaler scale-downs proceed in dev and prod, while each component keeps at least one pod during voluntary disruptions where it runs more than one.
recovery: If Argo CD shows the PDB OutOfSync after the merge, sync the app — never kubectl delete the PDB to unblock a drain.
dont: Do not kubectl delete pdb to unblock an upgrade
Do not remove the budgets altogether
Do not hard-code environment names in templates
hints: kubectl get pdb shows ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS. Compute it by hand for dev: what is the minimum number of API pods there?
With 1 replica, minAvailable: 1 allows 0 disruptions. maxUnavailable: 1 always allows one, whatever the replica count.
Helm docs: "Flow control" (if) and "Values files". Wrap each budget in {{- if .Values.pdb.enabled }} and read the budget from values.

interview.question: An AKS upgrade is stuck draining a node. How do you find the cause and fix it properly?
followUps: Why is a PDB on a single-replica deployment a trap?

debrief: In dev the HPA allows 1 API pod, so minAvailable: 1 meant ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS = 0: every drain (upgrade, autoscaler scale-down, node image update) waits forever, and AKS eventually fails the upgrade. maxUnavailable: 1 expresses the real intent ("never take more than one pod at a time") and keeps working at any replica count. The values switch keeps the policy configurable per environment without template branches on environment names.

validation.notes: Validated end to end offline: failing state on the current chart, automatic re-check on file change and commit, pass and celebration on a fixed copy.
